content.value: A behaviour each plugin implements to emit the edges its content contributes to the Content Graph — the projection dual of the search indexer.
is the per-plugin callback that turns a Document's payload into a list of directed edges. It is part of the Plugin Behaviour contract: each plugin that owns relational meaning implements

, and the host fans the call out across every active plugin when projecting content into the graph. Architecturally it mirrors the Indx Engine indexer — where Indx asks each surface "what text do you contribute to search?", the extractor asks "what edges do you contribute to the graph?" That symmetry with the Indx Retriever Seam is the whole design. It is the reason Search and the graph are two reads of one corpus: the same content the search indexer mines, the extractor mines for edges.

CORE itself is an extractor: it walks every Reference Field in the Schema and emits a reference edge per target. This is the Fresh Install Invariant — with all plugins disabled, the graph still has CORE reference edges and Blast Radius still works.
The Tasks Plugin extends the set: it projects
into the graph. Crucially these are hydrated onto the payload *before* the pure callback runs — the documented
trap is that an extractor reading off a stale, un-hydrated payload silently drops every dependency edge.
Extracted edges are not stored directly. They flow to the Edge Projector, an Oban Worker that materializes them into the Content Edges Table for Graph Traversal and the Graph View in LiveView Studio.
